t:
(a) Increase in Amount.—Section 2249c(b) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “$25,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall take effect on October 1, 2008, and shall apply with respect to fiscal years beginning on or after that date.

fable.w: This section only raises a dollar cap in an existing statute and sets an effective date. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 2249c(b) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “$25,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”.

opus.w: This section only raises a funding cap from $25,000,000 to $35,000,000 and says when the change takes effect. It does not require any comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders or right to sue. Citing and amending a statute is a technical change to a funding limit, not a process for public participation.
opus.s: Section 2249c(b) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “$25,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** The amendment and the cited statute section might tempt someone to look for a process involving outside parties. But the section only raises a dollar limit and sets an effective date. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, invited to comment, given a hearing or permitted to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends a statutory dollar limit for appropriations. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The change is an internal legislative adjustment to funding levels, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2249c(b) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “$25,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a dollar amount affects how funds are distributed, potentially impacting outside parties. However, the text itself contains no mechanism for outside consultation, comment, or participation. It is purely an internal budgetary adjustment.
